tasks.short: Prepare, discuss and update patient care plans with the healthcare team, coordinate actions and evaluate progress.

steps.what: Nurse reads the record and prepares notes per patient for the team meeting

loop.input: Nursing reports since the last meeting, plus structured vitals trends, scores, medication changes and lab results from the record.
loop.output: Per patient a short summary with bullets, each linked to the report it comes from.
loop.check: Each bullet cites a report of that patient in the period; values and doses must appear verbatim in the source; every flagged event (fall, pressure ulcer, early-warning trigger, medication change) must appear, else the patient is marked 'read full record'.
loop.stop: One draft and one retry per patient; on failure the nurse sees the structured list and raw reports.
loop.why_not_simpler: Nursing reports are free text by many colleagues; structured fields alone miss what happened.

steps.what: Physician, physiotherapist and dietitian contribute their findings in the meeting
Nurse consults with healthcare team members on each patient's care plans
Nurse updates the nursing care plan with agreed goals and actions
Nurse coordinates agreed actions with colleagues by phone and chat
Nurse evaluates the care plan against goals at the next review

tasks.design: Before the team meeting the electronic health record ({OTHER}) assembles per patient the structured trends and a drafted summary of nursing reports, each line linked to its source. Agreements are captured as actions with owner and due date; the nurse validates the care plan changes before they are written back, owners get the actions as tasks, and a goal view supports the next evaluation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing meetings meant reading every report, and agreements were re-typed and passed on by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Record tools now answer clinicians' questions on the record and scribes draft notes that clinicians validate, and care plan actions can become tasks.
tasks.still_hard: Summaries can miss or invent; the inspectorate expects providers to test, train and monitor generative tools, and team judgement cannot be shortened.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing the nursing view of the patient into the team and agreeing realistic goals with them.

ambition.what: Care plans evaluated against goals at every meeting for every patient, not only for the complex ones.

tasks.altitude: The nurse validates summaries and plan changes rather than compiling them; decisions stay with the team.

reach.task: Report patient progress to the team meeting
reach.learn: Whether the linked summary format suits therapy notes.

evidence.claim: A Dutch tool answers clinicians' questions on the patient record; its MDR certification is in progress.
In a European health system, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%) across 236,153 scribe notes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Care providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: know whether it is a medical device, assess risks, train, test and monitor after updates.
Decision-support software is usually MDR class IIa or higher; AI in such devices needing a notified body is high-risk under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from meeting preparation to the next evaluation; delivering care is outside.

Input contract: nursing reports written by nurses; vitals, scores, medication and lab results from the record; meeting agreements entered as actions with owner and due date by the nurse; fallback is reading the record.
The drafting runs inside the hospital's governed environment under a processing agreement.
Physician and therapist time is outside the nurse's savings.
unknowns: Whether the record system can export reports to a governed model service.
How many patients are discussed per meeting.
research_questions: How often does a draft miss a flagged event, measured over the first month of nurse corrections?

already_counted.description: Nurse checks the drafted summary against flagged events and source reports.
Nurse validates care plan changes generated from agreements.

incremental.description: Nurse records agreements as actions with owner and date and reports summary errors.
Clinical informatics monitors the summary step, audits samples and handles updates.

approvals.approved_version: Care plan changes as validated by the nurse before write-back; later edits create a new version to validate.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards where summaries often fail the check go back to reading the record, and meetings themselves do not shorten.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead a shift on the unit: check staffing, assign patients, brief and supervise assistants, solve gaps and report.

steps.what: Shift coordinator checks staffing against patient numbers and care needs on the unit
Shift coordinator assigns patients to nurses and less-skilled healthcare personnel
Shift coordinator briefs the team at the start of the shift
Shift coordinator supervises assistants' care and helps with complex care
Shift coordinator handles sick calls and asks the flex pool for replacements
Flex pool planner finds and sends a replacement
Shift coordinator reports unit status to the unit manager and bed management

tasks.design: A staffing view joins the roster with nursing workload scores per patient from the record ({OTHER}) and proposes a patient allocation by fixed rules (qualification, continuity, balanced workload) for the coordinator to change. Replacement requests go to the flex pool through the scheduling app, and a unit status view (beds, staffing, discharges) is shared with the unit manager and bed management.
tasks.previous_blocker: Staffing and allocation ran on whiteboards and phone calls because workload scores and rosters were in separate systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Records hold workload scores, scheduling apps take requests, and fixed allocation rules are simple code.
tasks.still_hard: Allocation depends on knowing colleagues and patients; rules that allocate by personal traits would be high-risk and are not used.
tasks.human_edge: Matching the right nurse to the right patient and keeping the team calm on a short-staffed shift.

ambition.what: Workload balanced across the team at every shift change, not only when someone complains.

tasks.altitude: The coordinator adjusts a proposal instead of building the allocation; supervision and decisions stay theirs.

reach.task: Receive patient assignments for the shift
reach.learn: Whether rule-based allocation feels fair to assistants.

evidence.claim: Systems fit to monitor attendance, behaviour or performance of staff need works council consent.
AI that allocates work based on personal traits or behaviour is high-risk under AI Act Annex III; fixed rules on qualification and workload are not AI.
A staffing view can join roster data with workload scores per patient.

assumptions: Boundary: one shift from staffing check to unit status report; rostering weeks ahead is outside.

Input contract: nursing workload score per patient recorded by nurses each shift in the record; roster and qualifications from the scheduling system kept by the unit planner; fallback is the whiteboard.
Workload views show patients and shifts, not individual nurse performance.
Flex pool planner time is outside the coordinator's savings.
unknowns: Whether workload scores are recorded per patient today.
How often sick calls hit a shift.
research_questions: Does rule-based allocation change perceived fairness and continuity of care?

already_counted.description: Coordinator reviews and adjusts the proposed allocation.

incremental.description: Coordinator corrects missing workload scores before allocation.
Unit planner keeps qualification data and allocation rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Small units with stable teams allocate in minutes already, so the proposal saves little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor all aspects of patient care on rounds, including diet, fluids and physical activity, act on changes and report.

steps.what: Nurse observes the patient on rounds: condition, pain, wounds and mobility
Nurse records diet intake, fluid balance and physical activity on bedside lists
Nurse reviews vitals, scores and lab results in the record
Nurse adjusts care and calls the dietitian, physiotherapist or doctor
Nurse writes the daily nursing report in the record

tasks.design: Configure bedside mobile entry for intake, fluids and mobility in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) and a per-patient monitoring view with fixed alerts, such as intake under half for two days suggesting a dietitian referral. A bounded model step drafts the daily nursing report from the nurse's spoken note and the day's entries, and the nurse validates it before it enters the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bedside lists were paper, and reports were typed at the end of the shift from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Records run on mobile devices, and scribes that clinicians validate are in use in Dutch care.
tasks.still_hard: Observation and judgement at the bedside stay human; drafted reports must be checked, and the inspectorate expects testing and monitoring.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a patient is not themselves today and acting before the numbers change.

ambition.what: Nutrition and mobility problems flagged the same day for every patient, so dietitian and physio referrals start earlier.

tasks.altitude: The nurse records at the bedside and validates reports; clinical decisions stay theirs and the doctor's.

reach.learn: Whether intake alerts lead to earlier referrals without overload.

evidence.claim: A Dutch scribe records the conversation, the clinician validates, and the note goes into the hospital record.
Self-estimated time per note fell 29% across 236,153 scribe notes in a European health system.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including medication errors from wrong registration.
The medical record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from rounds to the daily report; treatment decisions by doctors are outside.

Input contract: intake, fluid and mobility entries made by nurses and nursing assistants at the bedside; vitals from monitors; alert thresholds set by the ward's nurse specialist and dietitian; fallback is paper lists and typed reports.
Drafting runs in the hospital's governed environment.
Other professionals' time is outside the nurse's savings.
Vital signs are entered or validated by nurses as today; a monitor import is used only on wards where monitors are connected, and s3's saving comes from the one-screen view, not from the import.
s5 is part of recording and reporting changes in patients' condition, which sibling task 29-1141.00:1840 covers; its saving is counted there, so s5 keeps its full time here.
unknowns: Whether the ward has mobile devices for bedside entry.
Share of patients on intake or fluid monitoring.
research_questions: Do intake alerts shorten time to dietitian referral?

already_counted.description: Nurse reviews monitoring alerts and dismisses false ones.
Nurse validates the drafted daily report.

incremental.description: Nurse corrects bedside entries made late or wrongly.
Clinical informatics audits report samples and tunes alert thresholds.

approvals.approved_version: Daily nursing report text as validated by the nurse; later edits are a new version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards without bedside devices keep paper lists, and nurses who distrust drafts rewrite reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach patients and families about their condition and self-care, and develop group health education programmes.

steps.what: Nurse assesses what the patient and family know and need to learn
Nurse selects or writes health education leaflets for the patient

loop.input: Topics the nurse selects, the hospital's approved leaflets and vetted public patient information, and the patient's language and reading level.
loop.output: A personal information pack in plain language with the patient's own care plan items.
loop.check: Every sentence must cite a paragraph of an approved source or a care plan item; no advice beyond the care plan; reading-level score within the set band; the nurse approves before handing it over.
loop.stop: One redraft; then the nurse uses the standard leaflets.
loop.why_not_simpler: Combining several leaflets into one plain-language pack for one patient needs rewriting; a template can only staple them.

steps.what: Nurse instructs individuals and families, demonstrating skills such as injections or wound care
Nurse checks understanding by teach-back
Nurse records the education given with the short checklist in the record
Nurse agrees the programme's aims and content with colleagues
Nurse develops or updates the group health improvement programme from the module library
Patient education committee reviews and approves the programme materials
Nurse publishes the approved materials on the intranet and patient portal

tasks.design: A bounded model step assembles a personal plain-language information pack from the hospital's approved leaflets and vetted public patient information, citing a source paragraph for every sentence, and the nurse approves it before handing it over. Education given is recorded with a short checklist in the record ({OTHER}); group programmes are built from a module library in {DOCS} and published to the portal only after the committee approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packs were stapled together from generic leaflets, because rewriting for each patient took too long.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted, guideline-based patient information exists, and language models can rewrite it when each sentence must cite its source.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching skills and checking understanding stay hands-on; personal advice beyond the care plan needs a clinician.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a frightened patient can take in today and teaching the family to cope at home.

ambition.what: Patients with low literacy or another first language who get a pack at their level, not the standard leaflet.

tasks.altitude: The nurse approves packs rather than assembling them and spends the time teaching.

reach.learn: Which leaflets nurses combine most and where gaps are.

evidence.claim: A Dutch public patient information site gives guideline-based texts written with GP, specialist and patient organisations.
Patient education answers should be drafted only from vetted texts, each citing its paragraph, with personal advice signed off by a clinician.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including testing and monitoring.
Patient chatbots must disclose that they are AI; this design hands printed packs, not a chatbot.

assumptions: Boundary: from assessing education needs to materials published; clinical treatment is outside.
Input contract: approved leaflets kept by the patient education committee; vetted public texts the hospital licenses or links; care plan items from the record; fallback is the standard leaflets.
Committee time is outside the nurse's savings.
Teaching and teach-back do not change.
unknowns: Whether the hospital may reuse public patient texts in its own packs.
Languages most needed on the ward.
research_questions: Do personal packs improve teach-back results compared with standard leaflets?

already_counted.description: Nurse checks the assembled pack against the care plan before approving it.

incremental.description: Nurse reports pack errors and missing topics.
Committee keeps the approved source library current.

approvals.approved_version: The information pack as approved by the nurse for this patient; any change needs a new approval.
Programme materials as approved by the committee in s8; later edits need a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards with few education moments, or nurses who prefer standard leaflets, save little on preparation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse keeps bedside care, judgement, teaching and team decisions; compiling summaries, typing reports and building packs shift to validation.
skills_to_grow: Validating drafted summaries and reports quickly and critically
Recording care data at the bedside
Using rule-based allocation without losing judgement
role.ambitious_version: A nurse whose meetings, shifts and teaching start from checked drafts, spending the time saved with patients and families.
